title: Amarnath Cave Temple
geometryBasis: The named and Wikidata-linked OpenStreetMap cave entrance fixes the shrine’s site by its mouth. The Divisional Commissioner records the aperture as about 40 yards wide and 75 feet high, with a descending recess about 80 feet deep.
sectionBasis: Gangadhar Tambe’s cleared Qualla views establish the stepped shrine terrace, scalloped limestone aperture, roof fracture and seasonal interior ice pillar. The cave inventory independently describes the south-facing opening and the valley rock is reported as bedded limestone with thin shale and slate.
limitations: The mapped cave mouth and approximate government measurements provide the nominal opening scale. Rock surfaces, exact terrace grades, interior depth and fittings are reconstructed from two photographs and coarse native elevation data.

The scene shows a pilgrimage-season ice formation and a simplified historic terrace. Temporary shelters, people, modern crowd-management fittings, and deeper cave details are outside the modeled scope.
A small reversible viewer opening removes terrain only at the represented cave void. The independent unmasked source terrain remains unchanged and was captured separately.
